cards.title: A video call is still a doctor visit
cards.body: Treat it like one. A quiet room and a bit of prep make a teleconsult far more useful than a shaky call from the scooter parking.

cards.title: Fix the basics ten minutes early
cards.body: Charged phone, good network, volume up, camera lens wiped. If Nani is the patient, sit beside her so she can hear and you can help.

cards.title: Find light, then find quiet
cards.body: Face a window or a lamp so the doctor can see clearly. Turn off the TV. The pressure cooker whistle can wait.

cards.title: Keep everything within arm's reach
cards.body: Medicine strips, the last prescription, recent reports and home readings. You will be asked to hold things up, so keep them ready.

cards.title: Send reports before, not during
cards.body: If the platform lets you share files, upload clear photos ahead of the call. Reading a report off a wobbly screen wastes everyone's time.

cards.title: Write the advice down as it's said
cards.body: Ask the doctor to repeat medicine names and timings. Confirm you'll get a written prescription, and check it before the call ends.

cards.title: Know when video is not enough
cards.body: Teleconsults suit many follow-ups. For chest pain, sudden weakness on one side, confusion, trouble breathing or fainting, skip the call and get urgent help on 112.

takeaway: Good light, a quiet room, everything at hand, reports shared early and advice written down make a teleconsult work.
share: Teleconsult for Mummy? Charge the phone, find light, keep medicines ready, write everything down.
